name: Vigil Aerial Wing (VA-1 Belfry, VA-2 Angelus, VA-3 Knell)

scale.label: 1:56 (30 mm heroic Vigil line)
scale.note: Vehicle-tier ratio: model mm = in-world mm / 56 (17.86 mm per metre); heroic exaggeration only where a feature would not print (see exaggerations).

printer: 8K 7-inch class MSLA, build volume 153.36 x 77.76 x 165 mm (tools/mcpcheck.py PRINTERS)
frame: mm, z up, every airframe faces -y (its left side on +x). Belfry: origin at the rotor-arm plane centre. Angelus: origin on the main-rotor axis, z = 0 at the skid bottoms. Knell: origin at its chosen CG (flight-stem socket axis) on the wing mid-plane. Bases: z = 0 at the underside, centre at the origin. Wayfarer interface numbers are in the Wayfarer frame (x forward, y left, z up).

stem.rod_note: 1.6 mm clear acrylic rod cut to 38 mm fits every flight socket (1.8 mm glue-fit bores); the tether base uses the same stem as the tether cable.

roof_flat_zone.note: 0.25 mm ray-cast grid: roof plane z 38.5; engine-deck louvre slots (0.5 wide, 0.6 deep) at x 36.5 / 38.5 / 40.5 for y -14.25..-7; flat strip x 41..47 (to the glacis), y -17..-2; smoke dischargers at y <= -18 for x 28-35

catalog.revision_note: resin aerial wing: Belfry heavy-lift coaxial hexacopter (flying or tethered), Angelus observation helicopter + separate rotors, Knell flying-wing loitering UAV + rail launcher (tripod or Wayfarer roof pad), 7 loadout bits, stems, 40/50 mm bases
catalog.base: 50 mm (Belfry, Angelus, tether station) and 40 mm (Knell) round x 4 mm, 5 x 2 mm magnet pocket vented to the rim; flight bases carry a 10 or 15 deg raked 1.8 mm stem socket, the tether station a vertical one
catalog.description: The Vigil aerial wing: VA-1 Belfry, a heavy-lift coaxial hexacopter with a chin gimbal, swappable masts (EO ball, relay, radar) and belly loads (EO turret, SAR pod, twin glide munitions, cargo pod), flown on a stem or tethered to its spool-and-generator station; VA-2 Angelus, an unmanned observation helicopter with separate main and tail rotors; VA-3 Knell, a flying-wing loitering munition with a rail launcher that stands on a tripod or plugs onto the Wayfarer APC roof.

buildNotes: Flight stem: printed 1.6 mm resin, or a 1.6 mm clear acrylic rod cut to 38 mm; it seats 3 mm into the base socket and 2 mm into the airframe's 1.8 mm belly socket (glue).

Belfry: one piece with its 12 props. Mast socket (1.2 mm D-flat) takes VL-10 EO ball, VL-11 relay or VL-12 radar; belly hardpoint (1.6 mm D-flat, on the CG) takes VL-01 EO turret, VL-02 SAR pod, VL-03 twin munitions or VL-04 cargo pod. Every load clears the skid plane and the flying stem.
Tethered Belfry: put the stem in the tether-station fairlead (vertical socket) instead of a flight base: the stem reads as the tether cable. Print a second Belfry to field both versions.

Angelus: slide the main rotor (1.6 bore) onto the 1.4 mm mast pin and the tail rotor (1.2 bore) onto the 1.0 mm pin on the left of the fin; set any blade angle, then glue. Both rotors print flat on the plate with no supports.
Knell: flies on the 40 mm base (15 deg dive) or sits on the launcher shuttle pin (its stem socket). The launcher's 2.0 mm D-flat peg plugs into the tripod or into the roof pad.

Wayfarer roof: glue the 10 x 5.8 mm roof pad flat on the Wayfarer APC roof with its chevron pointing forward, centre at Wayfarer (x 44.0, y -12.0) on the z 38.5 roof plane: the flat strip between the engine-deck louvres and the glacis, left of the keel crest; nothing on the Wayfarer is modified. With the launcher fitted the RWS must not traverse through the measured blocked arc (see DESIGN-LOG / reports/build.json fits.wayfarer_roof).
Every other part prints on supports in the orientation miniature_support_plan picked (print/stl is already in that pose).
catalog.limitations: Procedural SDF sculpt, not a hand sculpt. Printability is a heuristic screen through unified-CAD-MCP, not a test print; print a tolerance coupon for the 0.1 mm glue fits. In-world sizing is heuristic (drone_* calculators). No STEP: FreeCAD is not installed on the build host (recorded as skipped / UNKNOWN). Rotor blades are 0.8-0.9 mm resin: handle with care.
